Can you send the scenarios and effective $/1M with our mix? Also looping Tom for procurement visibility.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Great questions — quick answers and a short worked example below. I attached the pricing_estimates.xlsx and a one-pager (redwood_pricing_summary.pdf).

What Redwood counts as cached/hit and what reduces billing
- Prefix cache: we cache prefix KV (system prompt + instruction tokens and any deterministically repeatable context). If a request hits the prefix cache, Redwood does not re-run the full autoregressive generation from scratch for that prefix; however, generated tokens (the response tail) are still billed when produced. In practice this means we reduce the billed prompt tokens portion significantly if your prompts are repeatable, but response tokens driven by customer-specific context remain billed.

Worked example (using your numbers):
- Raw tokens/day = 15M
- Breakout: prefix tokens = 30% (4.5M), unique response tokens = 70% (10.5M)
- Scenario A (conservative): cache hit-rate = 20% of total calls => 20% of prefix tokens served from cache = 0.9M tokens saved/day
- Scenario B (optimistic): cache hit-rate = 40% => 1.8M prefix tokens saved/day

Net billed tokens/day:
- Scenario A: billed = 15M - 0.9M = 14.1M/day => ~423M/month
- Scenario B: billed = 15M - 1.8M = 13.2M/day => ~396M/month

Effective $ assumptions (example list price used as placeholder):
- List $: $25 / 1M tokens (input+output)
- Scenario A effective $/1M = $25 * (15M / 14.1M) ≈ $26.6/1M (because cache reduces billed tokens slightly)
- Scenario B effective $/1M = $25 * (15M / 13.2M) ≈ $28.4/1M

Note on directionality: If caching saves prompt tokens, effective $/1M can either go up or down relative to list depending on whether you normalize to raw application tokens or billed tokens. In our commercial conversations we typically quote effective $/1M relative to billed tokens (so a hit-rate reduces your absolute spend), but for deal comparability we can present both views. The attached sheet shows both normalizations.

Recommended next steps:
- Confirm which normalization your procurement prefers (cost per raw application tokens vs cost per billed tokens).
- If you want a tighter model, share a small sample of anonymized request logs (we can sign an NDA) and we’ll run a cacheability analysis — gives a realistic hit-rate and expected monthly savings.
- If the $7k£$12k budget is strictly per month, we can run a 90-day POC with caps and a trial discount to get you data.

Would you and Tom be available for a 30-min call Thursday to agree on the normalization and next steps?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary.pdf

- Pricing framing: recommend we prepare both (A) cost per raw application tokens and (B) cost per billed tokens. Procurement typically cares about billed spend; Growth cares about raw unit economics.
